$comment: Closed verb vocabulary for companion command names (ADR-0175). A wire name is <resource>.<verb>; the verb segment is one vocabulary verb optionally followed by a qualifier (set_bounds, read_chunk, list_pending). Add a verb here with a one-line definition before using it. Refused verbs name their replacement.

standard.list: Page through a collection. Input takes pageSize and pageToken, output is {items, nextPageToken}.
standard.get: Read one record by id, or the singleton the resource names.
standard.create: Create a record and return it.
standard.update: Partial update. An absent field is untouched, an explicit null clears it.
standard.delete: Remove a record. Repeating the call is a no-op.

custom.ack: Acknowledge receipt of a delivery or event.
custom.act: Perform a described action on a page or desktop surface.
custom.add: Append an entry to a list-shaped resource.
custom.adopt: Take ownership of an externally created resource.
custom.analyze: Run an analysis and store its result.
custom.apply: Apply a change set, edit, or configuration.
custom.archive: Move a record to the archive.
custom.attach: Attach the caller to a live session or channel.
custom.backfill: Compute historical records that were never written.
custom.begin: Open a bracketed span (a turn or transaction) that a matching end, settle, or commit closes.
custom.call: Invoke a named method on a runtime with arguments.
custom.cancel: End a terminating lifecycle: a task, run, job, upload, operation, or handoff.
custom.capture: Capture a snapshot, selection, or recording.
custom.clear: Empty a value, buffer, or credential slot.
custom.click: Click at a point or element.
custom.clone: Copy a repository or snapshot to a new location.
custom.close: Close a handle, window, panel, socket, or transfer.
custom.compact: Reduce a session or store while preserving meaning.
custom.control: Drive a lifecycle operation chosen by an argument (start, stop, restart).
custom.decide: Record a decision on a waiting item.
custom.detach: Detach the caller from a live session or channel.
custom.detect: Discover installed tooling or environment facts.
custom.discover: Find endpoints or peers on the network.
custom.dispatch: Route an item to its handler.
custom.download: Transfer bytes from the host to the caller or to local storage.
custom.emit: Emit an event into a stream.
custom.end: Close a bracketed span opened by begin.
custom.enqueue: Put an item on a queue.
custom.ensure: Create if absent, then return. Idempotent.
custom.evaluate: Evaluate a script in a page context.
custom.evict: Remove cached entries for a target.
custom.exec: Execute an ad-hoc command line or code string.
custom.export: Produce an external representation of records.
custom.fetch: Retrieve bytes from a remote origin over the network.
custom.finalize: Complete a staged change so it becomes live.
custom.find: Locate elements or text on a page.
custom.focus: Give keyboard focus to a surface.
custom.forget: Delete a memory or key on purpose.
custom.forward: Forward a message or log to a sink.
custom.has: Predicate: whether a value is present.
custom.import: Bring records in from an external representation.
custom.ingest: Feed content into a store or model.
custom.inspect: Read detailed diagnostic state of a resource.
custom.install: Put a package, binary, or extension in place.
custom.interrupt: Stop the current turn. The session survives.
custom.invalidate: Mark a cache or detection stale.
custom.invoke: Invoke a named callback, pattern, or RPC on a client-side runtime.
custom.issue: Issue a lease, credential, or ticket.
custom.load: Load an artifact into memory or a runtime.
custom.mark: Set a status flag on a record.
custom.migrate: Migrate stored data to a newer shape.
custom.move: Change the position, column, or container of a record.
custom.nack: Reject receipt of a delivery so it is retried.
custom.navigate: Load a URL or move through history in a browser surface.
custom.offer: Make an offer to a peer.
custom.open: Open a handle, window, panel, socket, or transfer.
custom.parse: Parse a document into structured content.
custom.pause: Suspend a lifecycle that can be resumed.
custom.pick: Choose an element at a point.
custom.poll: Take the next available items from a queue.
custom.press: Press keys or a mouse button.
custom.probe: Answer a yes-or-no or availability question without side effects.
custom.project: Produce a disposable projection of a durable record.
custom.publish: Broadcast a record or state to subscribers.
custom.pull: Receive remote records or state into the local copy.
custom.push: Send local records or state to a remote peer.
custom.query: Run a structured query and return matches.
custom.read: Read bytes or a document. read_chunk is a byte-range read with offset and length.
custom.realpath: Resolve a path to its canonical form.
custom.reattach: Re-attach the caller to a session it previously held.
custom.reconcile: Bring stored state and observed state into agreement.
custom.record: Record an observation, metric, or checkpoint.
custom.redeem: Exchange a one-time token for its content.
custom.refresh: Re-fetch a cached value from its source.
custom.register: Add an entry to a registry.
custom.release: Give up a lease, handle, or run slot.
custom.reload: Reload a page, plugin, or configuration in place.
custom.repair: Repair a damaged store or outbox in place.
custom.replay: Re-deliver recorded events or a delivery.
custom.report: Submit observations about a resource to the host.
custom.request: Send a raw request and return the response.
custom.requeue: Put an item back on a queue.
custom.reset: Reset state to a reference point.
custom.resize: Change the size of a window or surface.
custom.resolve: Settle a pending question, reference, or path into a concrete value.
custom.respond: Answer a request the host raised to the caller (a callback, decision, or bridge reply).
custom.restack: Rebase a branch stack onto its parents.
custom.restart: Stop then start a process or service.
custom.restore: Bring back a record or state from a saved copy.
custom.resume: Continue a paused or suspended lifecycle.
custom.retry: Re-run a failed step or delivery.
custom.reveal: Bring a window or panel to the front, or expose a file location.
custom.review: Review a draft and record the verdict.
custom.revoke: Invalidate a credential, grant, or ticket.
custom.rotate: Replace a secret or key with a new one.
custom.run: Execute a defined unit of work (a task, hook, script, or turn) to completion.
custom.screenshot: Capture an image of a surface.
custom.send: Deliver a message, prompt, or frame into a session or channel.
custom.set: Replace a value or a singleton wholesale.
custom.settle: Finalise a span by reconciling its outcome.
custom.snap: Snap a window to a placement.
custom.snapshot: Read a point-in-time composite of a resource.
custom.spawn: Start a child process or session and return its handle.
custom.start: Begin a restartable process, service, run, or capture.
custom.status: Read the lifecycle or health summary of a resource.
custom.stop: Halt a restartable process or service. force:true replaces the old kill.
custom.submit: Hand a completed form, result, or request to the host for processing.
custom.suspend: Suspend a resource so it stops acting until resumed.
custom.switch: Switch the active page or target.
custom.sync: Reconcile local and remote copies in both directions.
custom.take: Remove and return a pending item.
custom.truncate: Remove every record but keep the container.
custom.uninstall: Remove an installed package, binary, or extension.
custom.unload: Unload an artifact from memory or a runtime.
custom.unregister: Remove an entry from a registry.
custom.upload: Transfer bytes from the caller to the host.
custom.upsert: Create or replace a record keyed by its id.
custom.validate: Check a definition for correctness without applying it.
custom.verify: Check a signature or credential and report the result.
custom.wait: Block until a condition holds or a timeout elapses.
custom.watch: Subscribe to changes of a filesystem or workspace path.
custom.write: Write bytes or a document. write_chunk is a byte-range write with offset and length.

abort.note: allowed under git, where it is the domain word for an in-progress merge or sequencer

state.note: state is a resource noun (plugin.state.get), never a verb
